name: Memoh
use_label: A cloud computer for every agent
one_liner: An open-source platform that gives every AI agent its own cloud computer, running even when your laptop is closed.

text.why: Handing work to an agent means it needs somewhere to keep files, open the web and accumulate results. Memoh gives each agent its own workspace — filesystem, desktop, browser, network and long-term memory — that stays up when your own machine is off.
text.take: Built for the case where you hand over a long job and walk away. For a question or two, you do not need it.
build: Go under AGPL-3.0. Run the built-in agent with your own API keys, or host the Claude Code and Codex agents you already use inside a Memoh workspace, and talk to them through Telegram, Discord or the web UI.

who.role: People who leave research or repetitive work running with an agent, and teams juggling several at once.

start.text: Look at memoh.ai first, decide between self-hosting and signing up, then have your model API keys ready.

caveat: You pay for model usage yourself, since it runs on your own API keys, and AGPL-3.0 means a modified service must publish its source.

license.scope_text: Release source if you redistribute or host it as a service.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The Memoh interface showing per-agent workspaces alongside the chat view.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
